representation: minisign signature block (not an installer; no patch involved)
notes: SECURITY PROBE, NOT A SIZE MEASUREMENT. Most numeric fields of this schema do not apply and are null by the schema's own rule; the artifacts are two 41-byte strings standing in for two releases, because the question is about the signature block and not about the bytes it covers. QUESTION: is the minisign trusted comment authenticated against the specific artifact signature it ships with, well enough to carry release identity? WHY IT MATTERS: if yes, binding identity into the comment costs one existing key, one existing signature and one existing fetch, and the alternative (a second signing key over the manifest) can be rejected. RESULT: yes, for the three tamper cases the design depends on. Editing v:1.0.1 to v:9.9.9 inside the comment REJECTED; splicing release B's own genuine comment onto release A's signature REJECTED; presenting artifact A with release B's whole signature block REJECTED. All three fail in minisign_verify::PublicKey::verify, which is the same call tauri-plugin-updater already makes -- so this is not a new check being added at a new place, it is an existing check whose second half nobody was reading. MECHANISM (read, not inferred, at minisign-verify-0.2.5/src/lib.rs:334): the block carries global_sig = Ed25519(sk, artifact_sig || trusted_comment), so the comment is bound to that artifact's signature and not merely to the key. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: case 4 is accepted and must be. Serving genuinely-signed old artifact B with its own genuine comment saying v:1.0.0 passes verification, because both halves really were signed. Nothing in minisign refuses it; the version comparison against what the client is being told it is installing is what refuses it. This probe therefore supports the claim 'the comment is a trustworthy channel for release identity' and does NOT support 'freshness is authenticated'. Those are different properties and this experiment separates them deliberately. SCOPE: ephemeral generated keypair, unencrypted, in a scratch crate outside the repo; no repository or release key was used. Tree dirty because the Gate P1 harness changes were not yet committed, so this record cannot support a DEMONSTRATED ledger entry on its own -- the in-repo regression tests at crates/plugin/tests/release_identity_flow.rs assert the same properties on every CI run and are the durable evidence.
artifact_provenance: Standalone scratch crate (/private/tmp/tcprobe2) depending only on published minisign 0.7.9 and minisign-verify 0.2.5. It generates a fresh unencrypted keypair, signs two distinct byte strings with distinct delta-v1 trusted comments via minisign::sign(.., Some(comment), None), then mutates the resulting armoured blocks textually and re-verifies each through minisign_verify::PublicKey::verify. Full source and captured run are embedded in the raw log, so the run repeats from the log alone.

measurements.case_4_genuine_old_release_served_whole: ACCEPTED -- expected; refused by the identity check, not by minisign
